We checked the exam blocks against content/course-v2/registries/lanes/sd1.json. l2: 5 items, options a/b, per-ad band 9–26, every ad recounted: 11–13 words each. l1: 2 texts in [56, 92], t6 61 and t7 63 words, 5 R/F. sp1: Stichwörter, of which not all are needed. sp2: 2 topics, cards-ask. s1: 5 fields, situation text in [36, 48]. The cast was read against casts/series.json and casts/a1.json: Priya is a Rezeptionistin who speaks Malayalam, Englisch and Deutsch; Arjun is 31; Krause is 63 and the Hausmeister; Lehmann is 79, lives in the Erdgeschoss and has been there fifty years; Amal lives with Samir and Rania. verdict: The unit is close, but it does not exit in round 2. The round-1 blocker and all three r1 MAJORs are closed in the unit. The validator is green, and LEX-01 passes on every read surface. Both proofs now need German. Nora asks for the rooms, so cd.a1.wohnung-beschreiben is performed. The directional „ziehen in die …“ stands once, glossed, and nowhere a learner must produce it. All 99 keys are right, every grammatical tile order is accepted, and every exam block is exact to sd1.json, with every ad now inside the per-ad band. The scenes hold together: the video tour, the three neighbours, the Hausmeister's note, Olena's lamp and the Heft cliffhanger that u06 picks up. One MAJOR stops exit, and it is a grader class the u04 trail already met (F01). The S1 form is scored field by field by the item checker. It marks „2 Personen“ and „zwei Personen“ WRONG on the persons field, and „31 Jahre alt“ WRONG on Alter. The information is right, and the lane's own rubric (sd1-s1) and a Goethe examiner would give the point. u09 avoided the same trap only by hand-listing twelve variants. The fix belongs in checkItem, with a test, not in accepted[]. Ten minors follow. Seven are small unit edits: two echo keys (F02); a structured-input distractor that is true in the story (F03); the Sp1 model's missing Malayalam and unnamed Stadtteil (F04); ls2-mo, whose target the r1 rewrite no longer elicits (F05); an over-broad factual explanation with an early „kein“ on q01 (F06); three idiom slips (F07); two German labels outside the LEX-01 walk (F08). Four are held by owners: the rule-smith's LEX-01 gaps, including „willkommen“ read as will + kommen (F08); the rule cards (F09); the lexicon, spine and SCHEMA residue of r1-F04/F11/F12 (F10); and the GRM-04 false positives (F11). Once the unit edits are made and the checker rule is green, 3–4 owner-held minors remain, and the unit exits.

findings.problem: The S1 form is scored field by field, deterministically, by the item checker. For exact: 'number' the checker matches the digits and then holds the words around them to the accepted strings. So on f3, „2 Personen“ and „zwei Personen“ are marked WRONG, and the screen shows „2“. That is the most natural way to fill a persons field, with a word the learner knows at u05. „31 Jahre alt“ on f1 is marked WRONG too. The information is right in every case. The lane's own rubric (sd1-s1: „passende Angabe aus dem Text“, spelling only where meaning suffers) gives the point, and so would a Goethe examiner. §9.4 rates „a defensible second answer not accepted“ as MAJOR. This is the u04 r3-F01 and r5-F01 class (the real grader rejects correct German), which must not recur. It is a class and not a slip. u09 escaped it only by hand-listing twelve variants for one field, which is the list-widening CLAUDE.md rules out as the fix („the rule belongs in the checker … with a test“).
findings.fix: Checker (rule-smith, src/lib/course-v2/checkItem.js plus a test): a form_fill field with exact: 'number' is CORRECT when its digit value (or number word) equals the key's, and every other token is a frame word of that field. Frame words are the tokens of its accepted forms and labelDe, plus a closed unit list (Jahre, alt, Person, Personen, Leute, für, um, Uhr). With that rule u05 needs no change, and u09 f5 can shrink to [„6“, „sechs“]. Stop-gap, only if the unit must exit before the rule is green: add „2 Personen“ and „zwei Personen“ to f3 and „31 Jahre alt“ to f1, and remove them when the rule lands. The same rule should decide whether an exact: 'name' field may carry extra correct information. „Berliner Straße 21, Leipzig“ on f4 is WRONG today, although the only addition is the city.
findings.proposedRule: checkItem, form_fill + exact:'number': value match + frame tokens of the field ⇒ CORRECT. Fixtures: a1.1-u05 f3 „2 Personen“, „zwei Personen“ and f1 „31 Jahre alt“ are correct; f3 „3 Personen“ and f1 „13 Jahre alt“ stay wrong. A test takes every registered form field and asserts that „<key value> <unit word>“ is correct. The test runs over all registered courses (u02, u05, u09 and the ta2.s1 forms).
